clue.text: Bear under repaired end of bridge

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so the letters of 'under' are reassembled in a new order
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of 'bridge' is used

explanation.surface: A troll lurking under a bridge whose far end has just been patched up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' turns UNDER into ENDUR; the final E of 'bridge' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it or tolerate it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Selfish behaviour to gripe about

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters of 'to gripe' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about another person's selfishness.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is an activity done mainly to boost one's own self-importance.

clue.text: Evil spirit making November follow March

indicators.note: following puts the letter for November after the word for march

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A calendar quirk: some demon makes November come straight after March.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is a malevolent supernatural being, an evil spirit.

clue.text: End call, engagement being cancelled?

parts.note: an engagement ring stands for the engagement itself
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: A phone call cut short when a betrothal is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang up the telephone is to finish a call, a British idiom.

clue.text: Record spread of congestion

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
jam is a fruit spread for bread

explanation.surface: Someone noting how far a traffic jam stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockage of logs on a river gives its name to any congestion or deadlock.

clue.text: One's work here should bear fruit

definitions.text: One's work here should bear fruit

parts.words: One's work here should bear fruit
parts.note: the idiom for a successful effort is read literally: labour in this place produces apples or pears

explanation.surface: An encouraging remark about a workplace where efforts will pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees are grown in this plot, so a gardener's labour there literally yields fruit.

clue.text: Value of sacred book for fussy functionary

parts.note: Job is a book of the Bible, so its possessive gives the letters
worth means value

explanation.surface: Pricing a holy text, then calling someone a petty official.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an official who sticks rigidly to rules, from saying a task is more than their position would be worth.

clue.text: Chairman's supporters?

parts.note: the Chairman is Mao Zedong, so his followers are those who back his doctrine; the surface suggests backers of a company chair

explanation.surface: Allies of a committee chairman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mao Zedong was styled Chairman Mao, and adherents of his communist doctrine take his name.

clue.text: Put third at worst

definitions.meaning: in racing, finishing in the first three (or so) behind the winner

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to a bronze medal at the very least.
explanation.definitionFit: Put means positioned; in horse racing a runner finishing in the top places, usually first three, has this result.

clue.text: Hackneyed collection of jottings?

parts.note: read as a joke, a book of trite remarks; in fact the term names a personal notebook of quotations and notes, and 'hackneyed' means commonplace

explanation.surface: A sniffy verdict on someone's notebook of tired observations.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a notebook was a traditional scrapbook of quotations and passages copied out for later reference.

clue.text: Smile and leave American to Mexican

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Advice to grin and walk away from a cross-border encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Mexico and Latin America this word is slang for a foreigner, especially someone from the United States.

clue.text: Sensible to follow sourpuss, but not straightforwardly

indicators.note: following puts the word for 'sensible' after the word for 'sourpuss'

parts.note: a crab is a grumpy, sour-tempered person
wise means sensible

explanation.surface: Someone sensible trailing a grouch, but by a roundabout route.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs scuttle sideways, so moving this way means going sideways or indirectly.

clue.text: Unable to cope with a fork supper?

definitions.text: Unable to cope with a fork supper?

parts.words: Unable to cope with a fork supper?
parts.note: a fork supper is a buffet eaten with only a fork; someone who has always been given food on a spoon, i.e. mollycoddled, could not manage one

explanation.surface: A guest who fumbles at a buffet where only forks are provided.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given everything ready-made, like a baby fed by spoon, leaves a person unable to fend for themselves.

clue.text: In awkward position, sort of fine

definitions.meaning: put under pressure, as when asked a difficult question
a penalty charged immediately by an official rather than through court

explanation.surface: Someone in a tight spot who seems more or less all right.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pressured to answer or act, and also describes an instant penalty, such as for littering.

clue.text: It's Red Revolution, the worst

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of the two words before it are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A political jibe that a Communist uprising would be the worst outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful, so its superlative is the most dreadful, i.e. the worst.

clue.text: This boxer is chicken

definitions.meaning: a fighter in a light weight division, just above flyweight
a small breed of domestic fowl

explanation.surface: Calling a fighter a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: The light boxing division is named after the small, feisty breed of domestic fowl.

clue.text: Insect eating citrus for food

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the insect surrounds the fruit

parts.note: an ant is an insect
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: An insect nibbling a lemon or lime for its meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect' and 'citrus' are both specific examples standing in for the pieces, while 'food' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a formal word for nourishment or sustenance.

clue.text: Show inmate reforming, getting parole at last

indicators.note: reforming means forming again, so the letters of 'inmate' are reshaped
at last points to the final letter of 'parole'

explanation.surface: A prisoner turns over a new leaf and finally wins parole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges INMATE; add the final E of 'parole'.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon performance of a play or film is an example of a show.

clue.text: Weapon made by boy, no dove

parts.note: Tom is a boy's name
in politics a dove favours peace and a hawk favours war, so someone who is no dove is a hawk

explanation.surface: A boy fashioning a weapon, with no bird of peace involved.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light axe used as a tool and weapon by Native Americans.

clue.text: Force one's way through American street

parts.note: thru is the American informal spelling of through

explanation.surface: Pushing through a crowd along a US street.
explanation.definitionFit: To push forcibly through a crowd or obstacle is a sense of this verb.

clue.text: Transform one with a pain reliever

parts.note: to morph is to change form
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Turning a single pill into a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for morphine, a powerful painkilling drug.

clue.text: Member of scrum supports midweek match

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits beneath, so the scrum member comes after

parts.note: Wednesday, shortened to WED, is the middle of the week
a lock is a second-row forward in a rugby scrum

explanation.surface: A rugby player turning out for a midweek fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A match can be a marriage, and this word means the married state.

clue.text: Starve, if thrown out of such a hotel

indicators.note: thrown out suggests being tossed about, so the letters of 'Starve, if' land in a new order

explanation.surface: A guest warned they will go hungry if ejected from a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels are graded by stars, and the top grade is the most luxurious class.

clue.text: Stay on the wing

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a side is a flank or wing, as of a building or army

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep to the flank, perhaps on a football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay somewhere is to live or dwell there, a synonym.

clue.text: From south, excellent railway going to the North Country

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means travelling upwards, so these letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-class

explanation.surface: A train journey from the south up to the North Country of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to the North' reverses AIRY to YRIA. 'North Country' looks like one phrase but 'Country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation with Damascus as its capital.

clue.text: Stay calm to avoid sunburn

definitions.meaning: an idiom for not losing one's temper
taken literally, not removing one's top in the sun

explanation.surface: Advice for a hot day, with an idiom hiding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to remain unruffled; read literally it is staying covered up under strong sun.

clue.text: Stagger time with swimmer

parts.note: an otter is an aquatic mammal, a fine swimmer

explanation.surface: A swimmer and a stopwatch, perhaps a race with a staggered start.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger is to walk unsteadily, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Keen about demand for patterned material

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for 'keen' is read backwards

parts.note: mad means keen, as in mad about football
to ask is to request or demand

explanation.surface: Eager buyers making demands for fancy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' linking keenness to the demand, but it signals the turnaround of the keen word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a reversible woven fabric, often silk or linen, with a figured design.
